answer: Cross-chain identity anchoring: a new agent joins only by binding one-to-one to a seasoned account on another chain carrying months of real history and collateral; the registry verifies age, activity, and stake and rejects reused anchors. Each identity stands on a terrace of reputation built over time, which no script can fake overnight. When a fake is proven, its stake is slashed like an ember stomped out, so the farmer must forge each anchor from scratch with months of real activity: 10,000 sockpuppets cost 10,000 real histories, and farming economics collapse.
